The first release of Coastty, a macOS terminal built on Ghostty that keeps an eye on your coding agents.

- **Agent sidebar.** Every running agent with its attention state: Working, Blocked on a permission prompt, Done but not yet seen, or Idle. <kbd>⌘U</kbd> jumps to the agent that most needs you. Claude Code is the only agent detected so far.
- **Spaces.** Groups of tabs you switch between with <kbd>⌃⇧1</kbd> to <kbd>⌃⇧9</kbd> or from the sidebar.
- **Sessions that outlive the app.** `coastty-host` owns every pane, so quitting Coastty ends nothing. Reopen it and every terminal is where you left it.
- **Layout commands.** `coastty space`, `coastty tab` and `coastty pane` arrange Spaces, tabs and panes from any shell, for you, your scripts and your agents.

## Install

```sh
brew install --cask ehs5/coastty/coastty
```

Or download `Coastty.dmg` below and drag Coastty into Applications. Homebrew also puts the `coastty` command on your `PATH`.

## Approve the first launch

Coastty is not yet signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks the first launch, whether you installed with Homebrew or from the DMG.

1. Open Coastty. macOS says it could not verify that Coastty is free of malware. Choose **Done**.
2. Open **System Settings > Privacy & Security** and scroll down to **Security**. Next to the message that Coastty was blocked, click **Open Anyway**.
3. Confirm with your password or Touch ID, then choose **Open**.

Or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Coastty.app` in a terminal instead.

## Upgrading

`brew upgrade` installs new versions. macOS asks you to approve the launch again, with the same steps as above, because every build carries a new ad-hoc signature.
